clue.text: They build a nest on moss, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of a nest on moss could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A bird building its nest on a bed of moss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They build' sounds like birds at work, but the definition is the masons; 'perhaps' tells you to rearrange A NEST ON MOSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Masons who cut and lay stone are builders by trade.

clue.text: Dock is ship-shape

explanation.surface: A harbour dock kept neat and orderly.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock a tail is to cut it short; ship-shape means neat and in good order.

clue.text: Either way, it's high time

indicators.note: either way says the word reads identically forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Whichever way you look at it, the moment has come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High time' usually means 'long overdue'; here it is twelve o'clock, the sun at its highest.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is when the sun stands highest, so it is the high point of the day.

clue.text: See 22
One of the first people named in Somerset House

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words Somerset House

explanation.surface: Somerset House, the old London registry of births, lists one of the earliest names.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset House in London once held the national register of births, marriages and deaths, which suits the genealogy picture.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Adam and Eve's third son is among the earliest humans named.

clue.text: Being about fifty-one perhaps, I'm not without restriction

indicators.note: about signals that the letters gathered here are moved around

parts.note: LI is fifty-one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone aged about fifty-one insisting they feel no limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LI (Roman fifty-one) with IMNOT; 'Being' and 'perhaps' only link the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no cap or limit means being free of any restriction.

clue.text: Top chap is to cook French fries

indicators.note: to cook something is to fiddle or doctor it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A head chef sets out to fry some potatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' rearranges TOP CHAP IS TO; British 'chips' are American French fries.
explanation.definitionFit: Fried strips of potato are called fries in America and chips in Britain.

clue.text: Phone the bosses-they're responsible

parts.note: to ring someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: Ring the managers, since the blame lies with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Instigators of trouble are the ones held responsible for it.

clue.text: Translate into Italian

indicators.note: to translate is to change into another form, so the letters of into are shifted

explanation.surface: An instruction to render something in Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translate' rearranges INTO; the definition is a person, an Italian name.
explanation.definitionFit: Toni is an Italian given name, so it can stand for an Italian person.

clue.text: Lemon tart is ordered for the conductor

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new arrangement, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A lemon tart is requested for the bandleader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like placing a restaurant order, but it rearranges LEMON TART IS; Sir Simon Rattle is a British conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Simon Rattle is a famous British orchestral conductor.

clue.text: Criminal group go north of the border

explanation.surface: A band of crooks heading for Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang is a band of criminals; in Scots dialect, spoken north of the English border, to gang means to go.

clue.text: But a blunt question may incur it

definitions.text: But a blunt question may incur it

parts.words: But a blunt question may incur it
parts.note: plays on blunt versus its opposite: a blunt question may draw a reply that is curt and cutting

explanation.surface: Ask a blunt question and you may provoke a stinging reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A curt retort is the opposite of blunt in the cutting sense.

clue.text: Camping or sailing?

explanation.surface: A question of whether one is camping or out sailing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tents and sails are both made of canvas, so you are beneath it whether camping or sailing.

clue.text: They take the blow and shake in consequence

indicators.note: in consequence suggests the letters of shake in come out altered as a result

explanation.surface: Boxers absorb a punch and tremble as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They take the blow' suggests a punch; it means nose-blowing, and 'consequence' rearranges SHAKE IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Handkerchiefs are what people blow their noses into.

clue.text: A view that makes sense

explanation.surface: A pleasant view that seems logical.
explanation.definitionFit: A sight is something seen, a vista; it is also one of the five senses, vision.

clue.text: Is involved with women of attractive appearance

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of is and women are mixed together

explanation.surface: Someone who is in a relationship with women and looks good.
explanation.definitionFit: A charming, appealing look is a pleasing, endearing one.

clue.text: The point in question raised by a farmer

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: The key issue a farmer brings up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' suggests bringing up a topic, but it means grown as a crop.
explanation.definitionFit: A cereal crop is grown by farmers, and growing is raising.

clue.text: You're entitled to it, but it's not left to you

explanation.surface: What you are owed, rather than an inheritance.
explanation.definitionFit: An entitlement is a right; the opposite of left as a direction is right.

clue.text: It's used in casting part of a film

explanation.surface: Film casting, choosing actors for a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler casts a line from a winding spool; a spool of film is also one section of a movie.

clue.text: Slough farm building perhaps

explanation.surface: A barn in the town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, but here it is the verb meaning to cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: To slough is to cast off, as a snake does its skin; a hut on a farm is an outbuilding.

clue.text: Advanced to a crisis

parts.note: a head is a crisis, as in come to a head

explanation.surface: Things progressed until they reached a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Being forward or in front of others means having moved on, advanced.

clue.text: A notion to be cast as the Merchant of Venice

indicators.note: cast means thrown into a new shape, so the letters of a notion are rearranged

explanation.surface: An idea about whom to cast in a Shakespeare production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' suggests the theatre, but it rearranges A NOTION; Antonio is the title merchant in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's play the title role, the merchant who borrows from Shylock, is named Antonio.

clue.text: Fell and gave up

explanation.surface: Someone who tumbled and then quit.
explanation.definitionFit: Fell means fallen down; gave up means abandoned, as with a plan or habit.

clue.text: Itinerant craftsman in poetry

parts.note: a craftsman here is someone who sails a craft, a wandering seafarer, the hero of Coleridge's famous poem

explanation.surface: A travelling artisan who appears in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craftsman' suggests a carpenter or potter; read it as a man of a craft, a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's Rime tells of an old sailor wandering the seas and later the land telling his tale.

clue.text: Soldier on a horse or ship

explanation.surface: A soldier riding a horse or sailing in a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalryman is a trooper; a troopship carrying soldiers is also called one.

clue.text: Ecstatic aroma, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals a word that is heard rather than seen

explanation.surface: A rapturous perfume, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sent is slang for being transported with delight.

clue.text: All quiet in the reservoir

parts.note: the sum is the whole amount, all of it
p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet

explanation.surface: Everything is calm at the reservoir.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil sump in an engine is a well where liquid collects.

clue.text: Once put down, it can be served

explanation.surface: A document that, once signed, may be delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: Writ is an old past participle meaning written down; a legal order is served on someone.

clue.text: Flycatcher first became a Channel swimmer

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of became

explanation.surface: A bird called a flycatcher turned into a long-distance swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: Flycatcher is a bird name, but here it is a spider's web. Captain Matthew Webb first swam the English Channel in 1875.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Matthew Webb made the first recorded swim across the English Channel.

clue.text: Stays away?

parts.note: stays are supports such as corset bones or ship ropes; with them taken away, something has nothing propping it

explanation.surface: Someone keeping their distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays are props, so with them gone the thing is left without support.

clue.text: Forced to return the cheese

indicators.note: to return means to go back, so the word for forced runs backwards

parts.note: made means forced, as in made to do it

explanation.surface: Someone compelled to send back the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a round Dutch cheese with red wax.

clue.text: Weapon launcher in Navy port to be due for modification

indicators.note: modification means alteration, so the letters of port to be due are changed round

explanation.surface: A naval port awaiting a refit of its weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for modification' rearranges PORT TO BE DUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Warships fire torpedoes from a tube fitted in the hull.
